models_evaluated: Avoidable hospital event risk prediction model (Maryland Medicare FFS)

links.outcome: Calibration-type bias: true avoidable hospital event risk by race/sex at equal risk scores
links.effect: No race difference (ME = 0.0003, 95%CI -0.0003 to 0.0009); males slightly lower (ME = -0.0008, 95% CI -0.0013 to -0.0003); no sex difference in intervention target group (ME = 0.0002, 95% CI -0.0031 to 0.0036).
links.quote: We implemented a simple bias assessment methodology and found no evidence of meaningful race- or sex-based bias in this model.

models_evaluated: Predictive model of avoidable hospital (AH) events

links.outcome: Race- and sex-based differences in true AH events conditional on predicted risk
links.quote: AH event likelihood was lower in males when controlling for risk level; however, the effect was small (ME = -0.0008, 95% CI -0.0013 to -0.0003) and it did not differ by sex for the target group for intervention (ME = 0.0002, 95% CI -0.0031 to 0.0036).

models_evaluated: Unspecified predictive model of avoidable hospital events

links.outcome: difference in AH event risk by race
links.effect: Likelihood of experiencing an AH event did not differ by race when controlling for predicted risk (ME = 0.0003).
links.quote: Black patients had higher average risk scores than White patients; however, the likelihood of experiencing an AH event did not differ by race when controlling for predicted risk (Marginal Effect [ME] = 0.0003, 95%CI -0.0003 to 0.0009).
